# CLI

Every command `ceres` accepts. The table commands near the end have no hand-written
declaration at all, their whole surface being generated from the entity definitions,
so a table's flags and the filter keys it serves can never disagree.

Every command takes the global options, and an address argument accepts `all`, a
component address, or a selector matching several.

## Global Options

| Option | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--version` |  | Show the current Ceres version number and exit. |
| `--config` `PATH` |  | Use a specific Ceres configuration file, possibly outside the current working directory. |
| `--color` |  | Enable colorized output. |
| `--no-color` |  | Disable colorized output. |

## Commands

### `ceres run`

Start the engine as a foreground process.

| Option | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `<ADDRESSES>` |  | Addresses of components to run on startup. |
| `--watch` |  | Automatically restart the engine on code changes. |

### `ceres check`

Validate project configuration (ceres.yaml) for errors.

### `ceres reload`

Apply configuration changes.

### `ceres status`

Show engine and component statuses.

| Option | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `<ADDRESSES>` |  | Addresses of components to show the status of. |

### `ceres start`

Start components at the provided addresses.

| Option | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `<ADDRESSES>` | yes | Addresses of components to start. |

### `ceres stop`

Stop components at the provided addresses.

| Option | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `<ADDRESSES>` | yes | Addresses of components to stop. |

### `ceres enable`

Enable components at the provided addresses.

| Option | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `<ADDRESSES>` | yes | Addresses of components to enable. |

### `ceres disable`

Disable components at the provided addresses.

| Option | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `<ADDRESSES>` | yes | Addresses of components to disable. |

### `ceres up`

Start and enable components at the provided addresses.

| Option | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `<ADDRESSES>` | yes | Addresses of components to start and enable. |

### `ceres down`

Stop and disable components at the provided addresses.

| Option | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `<ADDRESSES>` | yes | Addresses of components to stop and disable. |

### `ceres console`

Commands for interacting with a project's web console.

#### `ceres console open`

Open the project's web console in a browser.

#### `ceres console url`

Write the project's web console URL to stdout.

### `ceres service`

Manage a user-level SystemD or LaunchD background service for this project.

#### `ceres service generate`

Generate a service definition file for this project.

| Option | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `<PATH>` |  | File path to write to. Standard output is used if not specified. |

#### `ceres service start`

Start the background service, creating and/or updating the service file as needed.

#### `ceres service stop`

Stop the background service, deleting the service file afterwards.

#### `ceres service status`

Show the status of the background service.

### `ceres database`

Manage the project database.

#### `ceres database ddl`

Show DDL commands used to initialize the database.

#### `ceres database shell`

Open an interactive database shell (psql or sqlite3) for the project database.

#### `ceres database clear`

Remove all data from the database. Tables and indexes are not removed, only truncated.

#### `ceres database migrate`

Apply pending database migrations.

| Option | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--yes` |  | Apply without prompting for confirmation. |

#### `ceres database migrations`

Show applied and pending database migrations.

### `ceres generate`

Generate various project resources.

#### `ceres generate openapi`

Generate up-to-date OpenAPI schema for the Ceres Rest API.

| Option | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--output` `PATH` |  | File path to write to. Standard output is used if not specified. |
| `--format` `FORMAT` |  | The output format. |
| `--indent` `INDENT` |  | Indentation width for JSON output. |

### `ceres alerts`

Manage alerts.

#### `ceres alerts select`

Retrieve alerts.

| Option | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `<FIELDS>` |  | Output only these fields, each optionally renamed as `field:alias`. |
| `-o`, `--output` `PATH` |  | Write to this file rather than standard output. |
| `-f`, `--format` `FORMAT` |  | Render as JSON lines, CSV, or a table. JSON lines unless --output names a file the shape can be read from. |
| `--field` `FIELD[:ALIAS]` |  | Output only this field, optionally renamed. Repeatable. |
| `--header` |  | Write a CSV header row, which is the default. `--no-header` omits it. |
| `--id` `VALUE` |  | Only alerts with this id. Repeat to match any of several. |
| `--address` `VALUE` |  | Only alerts with this address. Repeat to match any of several. |
| `--root` `VALUE` |  | Resolve relative address selectors against this address. |
| `--timestamp` `VALUE` |  | Only alerts with this timestamp. Repeat to match any of several. |
| `--after` `VALUE` |  | Only alerts recorded at or after this time. |
| `--before` `VALUE` |  | Only alerts recorded before this time. |
| `--timespan` `VALUE` |  | Only alerts inside this span, as two times or a time and a duration. |
| `--max-age` `VALUE` |  | Only alerts newer than this, as a duration like `2h` or `P1D`. |
| `--min-age` `VALUE` |  | Only alerts older than this, as a duration like `2h` or `P1D`. |
| `--after-hour` `VALUE` |  | Only alerts recorded at or after this hour of the day, whatever the date. |
| `--before-hour` `VALUE` |  | Only alerts recorded before this hour of the day, whatever the date. |
| `--after-minute` `VALUE` |  | Only alerts recorded at or after this minute of the day, whatever the date. |
| `--before-minute` `VALUE` |  | Only alerts recorded before this minute of the day, whatever the date. |
| `--subsample-every` `VALUE` |  | Thin the result, keeping one row per interval. |
| `--subsample` `VALUE` |  | Thin the result, keeping one row per interval. |
| `--subsample-select` `VALUE` |  | Thin the result, keeping one row per interval. |
| `--level` `VALUE` |  | Only alerts with this level. Repeat to match any of several. |
| `--min-level` `VALUE` |  | Only alerts whose level is at or above this. |
| `--max-level` `VALUE` |  | Only alerts whose level is at or below this. |
| `--type` `VALUE` |  | Only alerts with this type. Repeat to match any of several. |
| `--type-contains` `VALUE` |  | Only alerts whose type contains this. |
| `--type-prefix` `VALUE` |  | Only alerts whose type starts with this. |
| `--type-suffix` `VALUE` |  | Only alerts whose type ends with this. |
| `--data-contains` `VALUE` |  | Only alerts whose data contains this. |
| `--data-prefix` `VALUE` |  | Only alerts whose data starts with this. |
| `--data-suffix` `VALUE` |  | Only alerts whose data ends with this. |
| `--order` `VALUE` |  | Sort by this field, `field:desc` to reverse. Repeatable. |
| `--limit` `VALUE` |  | Return at most this many alerts. |
| `--offset` `VALUE` |  | Skip this many alerts before returning any. |
| `--or` `VALUE` |  | Only alerts matching any of these subfilters, as a JSON or YAML list. |
| `--and` `VALUE` |  | Only alerts matching all of these subfilters, as a JSON or YAML list. |

#### `ceres alerts load`

Load alerts from a file, reporting how many.

| Option | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `<PATH>` | yes | The file to read alerts from. |
| `--format` `FORMAT` |  | The file's shape. Inferred from its extension when unset. |
| `--on-conflict` `MODE` |  | What to do about a row whose key already exists. |
